title: School English (Grades 2-5)
description: Foundational written English for young learners, aligned to the NCERT primary-English arc: letter sounds and naming words up through tenses, paragraphs, story- and letter-writing. Grades 2 to 5.

nodes.title: Letters and Their Sounds
nodes.skill: Match a letter to its beginning sound and write a word that starts with it.
nodes.teach_focus: Letter-sound mapping; one clear example word per letter. Provide the letter in text, do NOT ask them to find or look at a letter.
nodes.success_criteria: Writes a correct word starting with the given letter's sound.
nodes.bridge_focus: Just say one word that starts with the letter (e.g. b -> ball).

bridge_exercises.sentence: The word 'ball' starts with the letter ___.
bridge_exercises.hint: the first letter of 'ball'
bridge_exercises.context: Maps a known word back to its beginning letter — the easiest first step.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which word starts with the letter 'm'?
bridge_exercises.hint: say each word slowly and listen to the first sound
bridge_exercises.context: Moves from naming a letter to picking the word with that sound.

nodes.title: Naming Words (Nouns)
nodes.skill: Name people, animals, places, and things with the correct naming word.
nodes.teach_focus: Nouns as names; sort words into person/animal/place/thing. Do NOT ask them to look at a picture.
nodes.success_criteria: Gives 3+ correct naming words for a given text category.
nodes.bridge_focus: Name just one thing you can see around you.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Apple, dog, and school are all ___ words because they name things.
bridge_exercises.hint: the kind of word that names a person, animal, place, or thing
bridge_exercises.context: Names the category before asking the learner to produce one.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which one is a naming word (a noun)?
bridge_exercises.hint: which word names a place you can go to?
bridge_exercises.context: Sorts a naming word out from an action word and a describing word.

exemplars: Person: teacher. Animal: cat. Place: park. Thing: book.
Three naming words are dog, garden, and pencil.

nodes.title: Make a Simple Sentence
nodes.skill: Join a naming word and a doing word into one complete sentence.
nodes.teach_focus: A sentence needs who + what they do; capital letter and full stop.
nodes.success_criteria: One complete sentence with a capital letter and a full stop.

bridge_exercises.sentence: The cat ___.
bridge_exercises.hint: add a doing word (a verb) like runs or sleeps
bridge_exercises.context: Supplies the naming word so the learner only adds the action.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which one is a complete sentence?
bridge_exercises.hint: a sentence needs WHO and WHAT they do, plus a full stop
bridge_exercises.context: Tells a full sentence apart from a fragment.

nodes.title: This, That, These, Those
nodes.skill: Use this/that/these/those correctly to refer to near and far things.
nodes.teach_focus: This/these for near, that/those for far; singular vs plural.
nodes.bridge_focus: Say 'This is a ___' about something next to you.

bridge_exercises.sentence: ___ is a book. The book is right here, next to me.
bridge_exercises.hint: near + one thing: this or that?
bridge_exercises.context: Anchors the near + singular choice before mixing in plurals.

bridge_exercises.sentence: The balls are far away. Which sentence is correct?
bridge_exercises.hint: far + many things
bridge_exercises.context: Tests far + plural, the hardest of the four forms.

nodes.title: Action Words (Verbs)
nodes.skill: Pick the action word that tells what someone is doing.
nodes.teach_focus: Verbs as doing words; choose the right verb for an action.
nodes.success_criteria: Writes a sentence using a correct, fitting action word.
nodes.bridge_focus: Tell me one thing you can DO (run, eat, jump).

bridge_exercises.sentence: Birds ___ in the sky.
bridge_exercises.hint: an action word (verb) for what birds do in the air
bridge_exercises.context: A strong picture cues one obvious action word.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which word is an action word (a verb)?
bridge_exercises.hint: which word is something you can DO?
bridge_exercises.context: Sorts a verb out from a naming word and a describing word.

nodes.title: Describing Words (Adjectives)
nodes.skill: Add a describing word to tell more about a naming word.
nodes.teach_focus: Adjectives describe size/colour/feeling; place before the noun.
nodes.success_criteria: Uses a fitting adjective in a sentence ('a big red ball').
nodes.bridge_focus: Add one describing word to 'a ___ dog'.

bridge_exercises.sentence: a ___ dog
bridge_exercises.hint: a describing word for its size or colour
bridge_exercises.context: Open slot before the noun — exactly where an adjective goes.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which word DESCRIBES the ball?
bridge_exercises.hint: which word tells you more about how the ball looks?
bridge_exercises.context: Picks the adjective out from a noun and a verb.

nodes.title: What Is Happening Now
nodes.skill: Use the present tense to say what is happening now or every day.
nodes.teach_focus: Present simple; add -s for he/she/it (she runs, they run).
nodes.success_criteria: A correct present-tense sentence with right verb form.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Every day I ___ to school.
bridge_exercises.hint: a present-tense action word (for 'I', no -s)
bridge_exercises.context: The 'I' form needs no -s — the simplest present form.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Choose the correct present tense: 'He ___ football.'
bridge_exercises.hint: he / she / it adds -s
bridge_exercises.context: Targets the he/she/it -s rule, the usual present-tense slip.

exemplars: Every day I read a book.
She drinks milk in the morning.

nodes.title: Asking Questions
nodes.skill: Form a simple question using what/where/who/when and a question mark.
nodes.teach_focus: Question words; word order; end with a question mark.
nodes.success_criteria: A correct question with a question word and a '?'.
nodes.bridge_focus: Turn 'It is a dog' into a question: 'Is it a dog?'

bridge_exercises.sentence: ___ is your name?
bridge_exercises.hint: the question word that asks about a name
bridge_exercises.context: Supplies the question shape so only the question word is missing.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which one is a correct question?
bridge_exercises.hint: a question has the right word order and ends with '?'
bridge_exercises.context: Tests question word order, not just the question mark.

nodes.title: What Happened Before
nodes.skill: Use the past tense to tell about something that already happened.
nodes.success_criteria: A correct past-tense sentence about a finished action.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Yesterday I ___ to the park. (go)
bridge_exercises.hint: the past tense of 'go'
bridge_exercises.context: A common irregular cued directly by the base verb in brackets.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Choose the past tense: 'She ___ an apple.'
bridge_exercises.hint: which word shows it already happened?
bridge_exercises.context: Targets eat -> ate, a high-frequency irregular.

exemplars: We watched a film last night.

nodes.title: One and Many; a / an / the
nodes.skill: Make plurals correctly and choose a, an, or the.
nodes.teach_focus: Plural -s/-es; 'an' before vowel sounds; 'the' for a known thing.
nodes.success_criteria: Correct plural and correct article in a sentence.
nodes.bridge_focus: Add a or an: '___ apple', '___ book'.

bridge_exercises.sentence: I see two ___. (more than one cat)
bridge_exercises.hint: the plural of 'cat'
bridge_exercises.context: Simplest plural: just add -s.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Choose the right word: '___ apple'.
bridge_exercises.hint: use 'an' before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u)
bridge_exercises.context: Targets a/an before a vowel sound, the usual article slip.

nodes.title: Joining Words (and, but, because)
nodes.skill: Join two ideas into one sentence using and, but, or because.
nodes.teach_focus: and to add, but to contrast, because to give a reason.
nodes.success_criteria: One joined sentence using a fitting joining word.
nodes.bridge_focus: Join with 'and': 'I have a pen. I have a book.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: I was tired, ___ I finished my homework.
bridge_exercises.hint: a joining word that shows a contrast (a surprise)
bridge_exercises.context: The contrast meaning points to one joining word.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Join with a reason: 'I am happy ___ it is my birthday.'
bridge_exercises.hint: which joining word gives a REASON?
bridge_exercises.context: Chooses 'because' for cause, contrasting with 'and' / 'or'.

exemplars: I have a pen and a book.
I like tea but not coffee.
We stayed home because it rained.

nodes.title: Write a Short Paragraph
nodes.skill: Write 3-4 connected sentences on one topic.
nodes.teach_focus: One topic; sentences in order; each starts capital, ends full stop.
nodes.success_criteria: 3+ sentences that stay on one topic and connect.
nodes.bridge_focus: Write just two sentences about your favourite animal.

bridge_exercises.sentence: My favourite animal is the dog. A dog is ___ and loves to play.
bridge_exercises.hint: a describing word for a friendly pet
bridge_exercises.context: Adds one supporting sentence to a given topic sentence.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Your paragraph is about 'my school'. Which sentence stays ON the topic?
bridge_exercises.hint: which sentence is about school?
bridge_exercises.context: Teaches topic unity — keeping every sentence on one subject.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: My school has a big playground.
options: My school has a big playground.

exemplars: My favourite animal is the cat. It is soft and playful. It drinks milk and sleeps a lot. I love my cat.

nodes.title: Past, Present, and Future
nodes.skill: Choose the right tense for past, present, or future in a sentence.
nodes.teach_focus: Match time words to tense; 'will' for the future.
nodes.success_criteria: Three sentences, one each for past, present, future, all correct.
nodes.bridge_focus: Say what you WILL do tomorrow: 'Tomorrow I will ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: Tomorrow I ___ visit my grandmother.
bridge_exercises.hint: the little word that shows the future
bridge_exercises.context: The time word 'tomorrow' cues the future marker 'will'.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which sentence is in the FUTURE tense?
bridge_exercises.hint: which one has not happened yet?
bridge_exercises.context: Sorts future from past and present of the same verb.

exemplars: Yesterday I played. Today I read. Tomorrow I will swim.

nodes.title: Where Things Are (Prepositions)
nodes.skill: Use in/on/under/between to say where something is.
nodes.teach_focus: Position words; match the preposition to the actual place.
nodes.success_criteria: A sentence with a correct preposition of place.

bridge_exercises.sentence: The book is ___ the table. It is resting on top.
bridge_exercises.hint: a position word for 'on top of'
bridge_exercises.context: The 'on top' clue points to one preposition.

bridge_exercises.sentence: The cat is hiding ___ the box (inside it).
bridge_exercises.hint: which word means 'inside'?
bridge_exercises.context: Distinguishes in / on / under by the actual position.

exemplars: The ball is under the chair.
The cat sat between two boxes.

nodes.title: Write a Short Story
nodes.skill: Write a tiny story with a beginning, middle, and end.
nodes.teach_focus: A character, what happened, how it ended; events in order.
nodes.success_criteria: A short story with a clear start, middle, and ending.
nodes.bridge_focus: Tell just the beginning: who is the story about?

bridge_exercises.sentence: Once upon a time, there was a little ___ who loved to explore.
bridge_exercises.hint: a character for the story (a naming word)
bridge_exercises.context: Gives the story opener so the learner only invents a character.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which sentence is a good story ENDING?
bridge_exercises.hint: an ending wraps the story up
bridge_exercises.context: Tells an ending apart from a beginning and a description.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Finally, they all went home happy.
options: One day, a dog found a bone.
Finally, they all went home happy.
The dog was big and brown.

exemplars: One day a little fox got lost in the forest. She followed a stream and met a kind owl. The owl showed her the way home, and she was safe at last.

nodes.title: Write a Friendly Letter
nodes.skill: Write a short informal letter with a greeting, message, and sign-off.
nodes.teach_focus: Dear ___, a short message, and 'Your friend, ___'.
nodes.success_criteria: A letter with a greeting, a clear message, and a sign-off.

bridge_exercises.sentence: ___ Riya, thank you for the lovely gift.
bridge_exercises.hint: the word that starts a friendly letter's greeting
bridge_exercises.context: Isolates the greeting word — the first part of a letter.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which is a good way to END a friendly letter?
bridge_exercises.hint: a sign-off comes last and gives your name
bridge_exercises.context: Picks a proper sign-off over a greeting or a question.

exemplars: Dear Anu, Thank you for the lovely gift. I hope you can visit me soon. Your friend, Meera
